headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,024 AS 3.4% GDP BEAT CEMENTS DECEMBER HIKE FEARS — Silver Drops 2.9% to $52.41 Two-Year Low
snippet: Spot gold fell to $4,024 on October 29 as a stronger-than-expected US Q3 GDP print of 3.4% revived Federal Reserve rate hike expectations for December, compounding the hawkish signal from two dissenting votes at the October 28 meeting. Silver dropped 2.9% to $52.41 — its lowest since 2024 — pushing the gold-silver ratio to approximately 76.8; USAGOLD flagged the afternoon GDP release as the key catalyst extending the precious metals selloff beyond the morning's losses.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SOARS 13%, CRITICAL METALS +12%, TMC +11% — Critical Minerals Sector Extends Win Streak to Third Day
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) surged 13% on October 29 as a broad critical minerals rally continued, joined by Critical Metals Corp (CRML, +12%) and The Metals Company (TMC, +11%). No company-specific news drove the gains; analysts attributed the sustained three-day sector bid to renewed US-China supply chain tension headlines and investor positioning ahead of expected Q4 policy decisions on domestic critical minerals production incentives.

headline: AI BOOM BUILDS URANIUM 'SUPER-CYCLE' — Reactor Builds Outpace New Mine Supply, Contract Price Tops 2007 Record at $96.50/lb
snippet: Mining Weekly's October 28 analysis warns that AI-driven data centre electricity demand is accelerating nuclear reactor construction at a pace global uranium mines cannot match, creating a structural supply deficit. The long-term uranium contract price closed September 2026 at $96.50/lb — above the all-time 2007 record of $95 — while spot sat at $89.63/lb; the impending expiry of the US waiver permitting Russian uranium imports at end-2027 adds a near-term supply squeeze to the structural growth story.

headline: VIOR GOLD OPENS KINEBIK WITH 5.32 g/t OVER 2.5m — Two Rigs Targeting Cameron Main Zone in 15,000m Quebec Campaign (TSXV:VIO)
snippet: Vior Gold (TSXV: VIO) released initial assays from its 15,000-metre 2026 drill program at Kinebik in Quebec, with best hole KN-26-008 returning 5.32 g/t gold over 2.5 metres at the high-priority Cameron Main zone — 40km northeast of Lebel-sur-Quévillon. Historical drilling by a prior operator returned 5.07 g/t Au over 2.8 metres in the same area; two rigs are now turning with additional assays expected through Q4.

headline: WORLD BANK LIFTS 2027 COPPER FORECAST 18% TO $13,000/T — New Mines Cannot Keep Pace With Grid and Data Centre Demand
snippet: The World Bank raised its 2027 copper price forecast by 18% to $13,000 per tonne in its October commodity markets update, citing sustained demand from power grids and AI data centres that new mine supply is forecast to undershoot. LME copper has traded near $14,432/t this week — up roughly 20% year-to-date — while global mine production fell 1% in the first seven months of 2026 according to the ICSG; the bank's upgrade still trails BMO Capital Markets' $14,675/t target for the same year.

headline: TRIFECTA GOLD RELEASES 2026 RYE YUKON ASSAYS — Six-Hole Tombstone Gold Belt Campaign Closes the Loop After August Drilling (TSXV:TG)
snippet: Trifecta Gold (TSXV: TG) published assay results on October 29 from its 2026 diamond drill program at the Rye Project in Yukon — six holes totalling 1,852 metres across eleven Tombstone Gold Belt targets, completed in August with results expected in early October. The 2025 program established the system as a Reduced Intrusion Related Gold System, including a silver-rich intercept of 1,465 g/t Ag over 1.97 metres; the 2026 hole-by-hole data is now in the market.

headline: LIONTOWN HOLDS 2026 OUTPUT TARGETS AS LITHIUM SITS 'FINELY BALANCED' — No Supply Curtailment Despite Price Weakness
snippet: Liontown Resources (ASX: LTR), the Western Australian spodumene producer, told investors it is "looking through" recent lithium price weakness and will not adjust its 2026 production schedule, describing the market as "finely balanced." Battery-grade lithium carbonate prices fell more than 15% from September 2026 highs following CATL's decision to return the Jianxiawo mine — the world's largest — to care and maintenance after Chinese regulators revoked its environmental approval. Liontown says demand from battery manufacturers remains intact.

headline: GOLDMAN HOLDS $4,900 YEAR-END GOLD TARGET; UBS CALLS $4,000 A 'STRUCTURAL FLOOR' — 10 Oversold Juniors Screen as Rebound Candidates
snippet: Goldman Sachs maintained its year-end 2026 gold price target of $4,900/oz despite the metal's 25% retreat from January highs, while UBS called $4,000 a structural support level backed by central bank and sovereign accumulation. A Finwire analysis identifies ten junior and mid-tier gold mining stocks now trading at RSI readings of 28–35 — extreme oversold territory — that could disproportionately outperform the metal if gold recovers toward consensus year-end targets; Wheaton Precious Metals, trading at a 37% discount to analyst consensus, is among those highlighted.
